\section{Fixed-ratio lower bound: theorem and proof architecture}

The probabilistic argument of Erd\H{o}s gives the classical exponential scale
for diagonal and fixed-ratio Ramsey lower bounds \cite{Erdos1947}.  Ma, Shen
and Xie recently obtained the first exponential improvement for
\(R(\ell,C\ell)\) at every fixed \(C>1\) \cite{MaShenXie2025}.  Hunter,
Milojevi\'c and Sudakov gave a Gaussian random-graph construction and stronger
quantitative estimates \cite{HMS2025}; Lin and Niu sharpened the truncated
Gaussian cumulant analysis \cite{LinNiu2026}.  Truncated Gaussian variance
proxies and cumulants also have an independent probabilistic literature
\cite{BarretoMarchalArbel2024}.

This part works inside the explicit HMS Appendix-B induction.  The new
ingredient is not history conditioning by itself---that is already present in
the cited constructions---but a deterministic nonexchangeable triangular
mean ledger.  A boundary derivative must normally match a projection weight
exactly.  We first show that this exact-merge requirement uniquely determines
the array and leaves no scalar optimization freedom.  We then retain the
negative quadratic term from strong concavity and intentionally permit a
small deterministic mismatch.  Square completion pays this residual and
creates a larger net gain.

\subsection{Main theorem}

For \(C>1\), let \(p_C\in(0,1/2)\) be the unique solution of
\[
 C=\frac{\log p_C}{\log(1-p_C)}.
\]
The parameters \(p,c,D,\omega_0\), the source quantities \(B_R(C)\) and
\(B_B(C)\), and the exact-CGF term \(G_*(C)\) are defined explicitly in
\cref{low:sec:setup}.  The theorem imports the four version-pinned conditional
probability, extraction, and blue-ledger items (S1), (S2), (S4), and (S5),
stated in \cref{low:ass:hms,low:ass:hms-tail}.  The weighted reverse-propagation rule
(S3) is proved locally in \cref{low:lem:weighted-reverse}, as are the one-step
nonuniform estimate, first-moment conversion, and red--blue comparison.

\begin{theorem}[Source-relative fixed-ratio bound]\label{low:thm:main-lower}
Fix the absolute source constant \(K\) used in \eqref{low:eq:source-K}.  Under
\cref{low:ass:hms,low:ass:hms-tail}, there exists \(C_0=C_0(K)>1\) such that, for each
fixed \(C\ge C_0\),
\[
\liminf_{\ell\to\infty}\frac1\ell
\log R(\ell,\lfloor C\ell\rfloor)
\ge
-\frac12\log p_C+\frac{B_R(C)}2+G_*(C)+\widehat H_*(C),
\tag{L1.1}\label{low:main:eq:1-1}
\]
where \(\widehat H_*(C)>0\) and
\[
 \widehat H_*(C)=\frac{1+o(1)}{64\log C}\qquad(C\to\infty).
 \tag{L1.2}\label{low:main:eq:1-2}
\]
The public coarsening \(B_R(C)/2\ge1/20\) may be substituted in \eqref{low:main:eq:1-1}.
\end{theorem}

The quantifiers are important: \(K\) is fixed first, then \(C\) is fixed
before \(\ell\to\infty\), and the proof does not give a numerical \(C_0(K)\).
The source contains unspecified
\(O(\cdot)\) and \(o(\cdot)\) constants, so an effective threshold cannot be
extracted from the pinned text alone.

\subsection{Contributions}

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item We prove rigidity of the exact-gradient triangular recursion.
\item We construct an adapted deterministic residual and prove a uniform
      full-box Hessian bound.
\item We compute the exact multiplicity of the residual and its square
      penalty.
\item We insert a three-factor H\"older decomposition without counting the
      old exact-CGF gain twice.
\item We propagate the ledger through reverse induction and quantify the
      perfect-sequence extraction loss.
\item We optimize a narrowly specified scalar residual class and obtain the
      leading coefficient \(1/64\).
\end{enumerate}

The result is stated as a source-relative strengthening.  A direct claim of
improvement over every printed final normalization in Lin--Niu would require
both expressions to be derived from one common terminal probability formula;
that comparison is not asserted here.
